title: Two doorway instances in the alpha namespace federate the shared conductor pool; one human can register at either doorway and content delivery works through both

vision_quotes.text: Humans register with multiple doorways — multi-registration = resiliency; flows doorway-agnostic.
Doorway is single-target dispatch — substrate moves bytes; doorway projects+caches; peer-iteration = regression.
P2P mesh is the hosting layer — peer-sharding IS hosting; doorway is optional web2 projection.
Doorway as peer registration point — peers register with doorway, not Holo's marketplace.

plan_deliverables.text: A second doorway pod (elohim-doorway-alpha-b) runs in the elohim-alpha namespace, deployed from the dev branch via the alpha pipeline. It serves the apex hostname elohim.host (and signal.elohim.host) with its own DOORWAY_ID 'apex-elohim-host' and its own MongoDB projection database 'doorway-alpha-b'. Both /health and /version respond green.

Doorway-A and doorway-B discover each other via FEDERATION_PEERS. Each one's /admin/federation/peers endpoint lists the other; the heartbeat task keeps the peer cache fresh; both doorways register themselves in the infrastructure zome as content publishers with overlapping capabilities (blob, html5_app).
plan_deliverables.source: doorway/doorway-service/src/services/federation.rs (existing); FEDERATION_PEERS env in alpha.yaml + alpha-b.yaml (this branch)

plan_deliverables.text: A new human can register an account at doorway-A (alpha.elohim.host) and the same identity is reachable when logging in at doorway-B (elohim.host) — custodial keys + agency context flow via the shared alpha conductor pool, not via shared MongoDB. Distinct MongoDB DBs prove the substrate is the source of truth.
plan_deliverables.source: Existing doorway custodial-key flow (auth_routes.rs); shared CONDUCTOR_URLS in alpha.yaml + alpha-b.yaml.

plan_deliverables.text: Content seeded into the alpha DHT (via the existing seeder against any human's conductor) is fetchable through both doorway-A and doorway-B at identical URL shapes (e.g. /blob/<hash>, /apps/<slug>, /lamad/concept/<id>). The two projection caches converge independently from the underlying DHT, demonstrating the doorway-as-projection vs. doorway-as-source story.
plan_deliverables.source: Existing projection layer (doorway-service/src/projection); independent MONGODB_DB values in alpha.yaml + alpha-b.yaml.

manifesto_anchors.why: Until a second doorway actually runs in production-shape topology, doorway-federation is a design diagram, not a substrate property. Federation must be observably true, not merely conceivable.

The 'doorway as OAuth relying party' frame is hollow if a user is locked to one doorway. Multi-doorway registration is the protocol's promise that no single doorway is gatekeeper — the human's identity lives on the substrate, not in any one gateway's MongoDB.

If a content URL only resolves at the doorway that ingested it, the protocol has accidentally re-created the same single-host coupling that web2 hosting imposes. Cross-doorway content delivery is the visible proof that the substrate, not any gateway, holds the content.

scenarios_missing.intent: Both doorways report each other as a federation peer at /admin/federation/peers within N seconds of pod-ready.
A human registers at doorway-A, then logs in at doorway-B; the second login produces a valid session for the same humanId (custodial key + agency context are substrate-derived, not MongoDB-derived).
Content seeded against matthew-alpha's conductor is reachable via both alpha.elohim.host/blob/<hash> AND elohim.host/blob/<hash> with byte-identical responses.

screenshot_targets.what_should_be_visible: alpha.elohim.host page shows a row for apex-elohim-host with last_heartbeat < 60s; the mirrored elohim.host page shows a row for alpha-elohim-host with last_heartbeat < 60s. Both rows show capabilities [blob, html5_app].

screenshot_targets.scenario: Account registered at A is reachable at B
screenshot_targets.what_should_be_visible: Login form at elohim.host accepts Susan's identifier (susan@apex-elohim-host or whatever doorway-B's suffix is), the auth flow returns a valid session for Susan's humanId — same humanId observed at the alpha conductor pool.
Identical landing page response from both hosts. Network panel shows distinct origin servers but identical content-hash header and body.

operator_cutover_steps.why: Frees the elohim.host apex hostname claim held by the (paused) prod elohim-app ingress so cert-manager can reissue the cert in elohim-alpha for doorway-alpha-b. The manifest file has been renamed to elohim-prod-paused.elohim.host so the next prod apply would not re-claim apex, but the live ingress on the cluster still holds the claim until manually deleted.

operator_cutover_steps.command: kubectl delete certificate -n elohim-prod elohim-site-tls-cert elohim-prod-paused-tls-cert 2>/dev/null || true
operator_cutover_steps.why: Optional — releases cert-manager's apex cert lock from elohim-prod. cert-manager will reissue elohim-host-apex-tls in elohim-alpha on the next doorway-alpha-b ingress reconcile. Safe to skip if the cert was never issued.
Triggers the orchestrator → elohim-edge pipeline, which now also deploys alpha-b.yaml as elohim-doorway-alpha-b. Watch the orchestrator build log for both doorway rollout-status calls succeeding.
Smoke-test that both doorways are reachable on their public hostnames. /health does not require auth.
Confirms doorway-B sees doorway-A in its peer cache. Mirror with /alpha doorway's admin endpoint to confirm the reverse direction.
